preconditions.expression: root is None or isinstance(root, TreeNode)
preconditions.description: The input `root` must be either a `TreeNode` instance or `None`, representing an empty tree.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= node.val <= 10**5 for node in [root] + [node.left for node in [root] if root] + [node.right for node in [root] if root] if node])
preconditions.description: Every node's value in the tree must be an integer between 1 and 10^5 (inclusive).

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(node.left, TreeNode) or node.left is None for node in [root] + [node.left for node in [root] if root] + [node.right for node in [root] if root] if node])
preconditions.description: Every node's `left` child must be either a `TreeNode` or `None`.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(node.right, TreeNode) or node.right is None for node in [root] + [node.left for node in [root] if root] + [node.right for node in [root] if root] if node])
preconditions.description: Every node's `right` child must be either a `TreeNode` or `None`.

postconditions.expression: len(return_value) == sum(1 for _ in [root] + [node.left for node in [root] if root] + [node.right for node in [root] if root] if node])
postconditions.description: The length of the returned list equals the total number of nodes in the tree (including `root`).

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= val <= 10**5 for val in return_value)
postconditions.description: Every value in the returned list is an integer between 1 and 10^5 (inclusive).

postconditions.expression: all(return_value.count(val) == sum(1 for node in [root] + [node.left for node in [root] if root] + [node.right for node in [root] if root] if node and node.val == val) for val in set(return_value))
postconditions.description: The returned list contains each node's value exactly as many times as it appears in the tree (accounting for duplicates).

postconditions.expression: all(return_value[i] == node.val for i, node in enumerate(inorder_traversal(root)))
postconditions.description: The returned list matches the inorder traversal (left-root-right) of the tree, where `inorder_traversal` is a hypothetical recursive helper function.
